newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices fall on March data.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices fall on March data.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds lost around 1/2 of a point in slow, late trade on Friday, hurt by the latest economic data for March that helped intensify concerns that the central bank again will raise rates.
Traders said that the big losses seen in fixed-income futures and cash Treasury bonds increased the lack of liquidity in the municipal market.
"Once it went down, I think they (traders) just buried their heads in their hats," one trader said.

The deal of the week, New York City's sale on Wednesday of $900 million of tax-exempt bonds, at first looked like it might resist the slide, but by late on Friday, the new debt had fully participated, traders said.

There was speculation that a decision by Moody's Investors Service to downgrade Syracuse, New York's rating to A1 from A3 could trigger yields to rise much as 10 basis points in its bonds, but traders noted that it might take time for any drop in price to work its way into the market as the bonds typically are not very liquid.

"I think it (the downgrade) would knock it down an 05, but realistically, as much as an 10," a trader said, explaining that he thought the market had been overpricing the bonds, and thus the bigger loss was more likely.
"They skipped A2, it's a big downgrade," he said, adding it now appeared other rating agencies also would downgrade Syracuse's debt.

Moody's said it took the action to highlight ongoing concerns about the town's long-term fiscal integrity, noting its general fund balance totaled a "very modest" $2.2 million, less than two percent of revenues.

"While narrow General Fund balances and Tax Anticipation Notes issuance represent more of the norm for many New York State cities, Syracuse's high degree of reliance on interfund borrowings and receivables could lead to a General Fund cash crunch and further weaken the city's credit position," the agency said, in prepared remarks.

Stronger economic data pushed fixed-income markets down sharply, with June Treasury bond futures sliding 23 ticks to 106-20/32, while the June municipal futures fell 26 ticks to 111-20/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 160 ticks.
The Labor Department said March producer prices slipped 0.1 percent overall, but the closely watched core rate jumped 0.4 percent.
And while the Commerce Department found a 0.2 percent rise in March retail sales, which was softer than economists had anticipated, January and February sales figures were revised upward.
February sales were revised to a gain of 1.5 percent, almost double the 0.8 percent rise first reported.

In the secondary market, North Carolina Medical Care Commission Hospital Revenues, Wake County, Hospital System of October 2026, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.98 percent, up five basis points.
Jefferson County, Alabama, Sewer Revenues of February 2023, which pay a 5-3/4 percent coupon, were bid at 96-1/4, down 1/4 of a point.
